reader.requirement: At --std 85, for every ALL, LEADING, CHARACTERS (TALLYING and REPLACING), FIRST and CONVERTING phrase of INSPECT formats 1-4 the compiler must refuse a second BEFORE or a second AFTER phrase on the same phrase, and accept at most one BEFORE and one AFTER in either order (with the GR8 b/c boundaries both applied).

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.InspectBeforeFromFirstEligiblePosition: at 85 a BEFORE boundary is found from the leftmost position (§1985:VI.6.18.4 GR8b), at 2023 from the first eligible position; governs the run-time meaning of a BEFORE+AFTER pair, not the SR4 count

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry/DialectBehavior in InspectBinder.cs and VersionConformancePass.cs (VisitInspectStatement gates only BACKWARD; VisitInspectConvertingPhrase only CONVERTING TO ALL); the inspectDelimiters grammar rule that enforces SR4 is not edition-gated.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the SR4 refusal is the grammar's at every edition (the BEFORE+AFTER run-time boundary differs by GR8b, which the probe's values confirm follow the 1985 text)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1125_inspect_printed_format_shapes covers printed-format shapes; a duplicate BEFORE or AFTER on each of the five phrase kinds and the run-time intersection of one BEFORE with one AFTER are not exercised

probes.expected: accepted with one BEFORE and one AFTER in both orders; S='AYAXAA Y' ALL 'A' AFTER 'X' BEFORE 'Y' is 0 by GR8b (BEFORE measured from the leftmost position), T='XAABAAYA' CHARACTERS 5, LEADING 2, FIRST/CONVERTING/CHARACTERS replace only positions in both boundaries

reader.notes: The one inspectDelimiters rule (BEFORE [AFTER] | AFTER [BEFORE]) is shared by every count, replacing and converting phrase, so a repeated BEFORE or AFTER ends the statement and draws COBOL2269 at every edition. The binder orders the pair by token index; the 85 arm of GR8b gives the boundaries the 1985 text prints.

refuter.evidence: cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.18.3 SR4  the text is in SR4. Probes at --std 85 on S='XABAYABZAB': n1 one ALL phrase with two literal-1 operands each carrying its own BEFORE/AFTER INITIAL, plus a second tally identifier with ALL and LEADING, accepted and printed '05 01' (C1: A at 2,4,6 before Z plus B at 7,10 after Y; C2: A at 9) as the left-to-right GRs give; n3 format 3 with one AFTER and one BEFORE in both orders on ALL, a second ALL operand pair and FIRST printed '03 XabaYAbzAB', correct; n2 two BEFORE INITIAL on one ALL refused COBOL2269; n4 two AFTER (second with INITIAL) on a REPLACING ALL pair refused COBOL2269; n5 CHARACTERS AFTER BEFORE AFTER refused COBOL2269. The optional INITIAL keyword does not let a duplicate through, and a second operand's own phrase is not miscounted as a duplicate.
